name: AND, OR, and NOT
desc: Covers the boolean value functions AND, OR, and NOT (NOR): one or more strict boolean operands, ordered short-circuit evaluation, numeric identifiers, nested functions, value-context operands and namespaces, match-context function boundaries, syntax, and failure/resource propagation. These functions return booleans; they do not perform host truthiness coercion or act as match combinators. Every case is independent of implementation availability.

tests.name: NOT
tests.desc: NOT is NOR over one or more boolean values, returning true only when every evaluated operand is false. It stops at the first true.

tests.name: Truth tables
tests.desc: All one- through four-operand boolean combinations test the result, including falsey booleans and multiple-operand NOR rather than NAND.

tests.name: Strict operand types
tests.desc: Every reached operand must be boolean; numbers, strings, null, objects, arrays, and dates are not coerced. A valid early decision may skip operands of any type.

tests.name: Short-circuit evaluation
tests.desc: Operands are evaluated in order only until the first decisive boolean or error. Valid FAIL and missing-reference expressions must be skipped after a decision; reached errors propagate. Unreached syntax may still be rejected statically.

tests.name: Decisive first operand skips missing reference
An earlier invalid operand is not rescued
Unreached syntax may be diagnosed statically
Negative probe cannot hide reached recursion
Value contexts and namespaces
tests.desc: Operands evaluate as values in the same caller scope. Match-expression operands produce booleans, while referenced arrays remain arrays. Nested lexical bindings and common expressions use invocation-time context.

tests.name: A matched group does not publish captures
Function boundaries in matching
tests.desc: The returned boolean is literal data when used as a pattern. Inner match-expression operands retain their ordinary HAS default rather than inheriting an outer exact mode. Alternate-target function patterns evaluate against the original caller NODE.

tests.name: A boolean result does not match a number
Syntax and fatal errors
tests.desc: Each function requires one or more operands. Empty argument lists and reached malformed expression syntax are INVALID_GRAFT, including inside negative matching probes.

tests.name: Negative probe cannot hide malformed syntax
